# Exterior Binding and Spine (1682 Edition)

This 17th-century volume is bound in light brown leather, showcasing a high level of craftsmanship through various decorative techniques. The binding utilizes <term>blind-tooling</term> <note>a technique where decorative patterns are impressed into leather using heated tools without the use of gold or pigment, creating a subtle, indented design</note> and <term>gold-tooling</term> <note>a process where gold leaf is pressed into the leather with heated tools to create a shimmering, decorative effect</note>.

The front cover is dominated by a large, central <term>lozenge</term>-shaped medallion <note>a diamond-shaped decorative ornament</note>. This central feature is blind-stamped with a symmetrical pattern of foliage and scrolls. A double-line blind-tooled border frames the entire cover. At each corner of the inner rectangle and at the midpoints of the vertical lines, the binder has placed small decorative <term>palmettes</term> or <term>fleurons</term> <note>small, flower-like or leaf-like stamps used to accent corners and borders</note>.

The spine is constructed with five prominent <term>raised bands</term> <note>the horizontal ridges on a book's spine where the leather covers the cords or "supports" used to sew the pages together</note>. These bands divide the spine into six compartments. 

*   The second compartment from the top contains a <term>spine label</term> <note>a piece of leather, often in a contrasting color, used to display the book's title</note> decorated with gold-tooling. 
*   The first, third, fifth, and sixth compartments are embellished with identical gold-tooled floral motifs.

The edges of the boards also show traces of decorative tooling, indicating the thoroughness of the book’s decoration.

# Preface to the READER.

## Dearly Beloved Reader.

Many years have already passed during which nothing but strife and quarreling has been heard throughout all of Christendom regarding matters of faith. For this reason, so many <term>Colleges and Universities<note>The original German "Collegia und Hohe Schulen" refers to the established academic and theological institutions of the 17th and 18th centuries.</note></term> have been established in the world, so many heavy books have been written about controversial opinions in theological matters, so many Councils have been assembled, and so many great teachers have been brought together in our time—and all of this with such great care, diligence, effort, and expense—and yet, until now, it has not been possible to prevent discord and division. The schisms and disputes within Christendom are now greater than they have ever been. How many controversial opinions are there among the theologians? How many people have separated from the Roman Church to maintain their own opinions? How many of them are still within it, who in

<summary>This preface introduces a reflection on the deep religious divisions and endless theological debates plaguing Christendom despite the efforts of universities and church councils. The author laments that academic and institutional efforts have failed to bring about unity or peace in matters of faith.</summary>
<keywords>Christendom, religious strife, theologians, Roman Church, Universities, Church Councils, sectarianism, Reformation era</keywords>

->P R E F A C E<-

their <term>divinity<note>The original German "Gottesgelahrtheit" refers to the formal academic study of theology.</note></term> do not agree, and meanwhile all together and each one individually base their opinions on certain verses of the Holy Scripture. Therefore, one cannot know which side to take in order to follow the right truth. God necessarily had to send us a new light to distinguish the true from the false, as well as true theology from that which is fabricated and newly invented through human judgment and diligence; this is what He seems to do in these dark times, wherein everyone is <term>groping about<note>The original "nach dem griffe wandelt" describes a person walking by touch, like one lost in total darkness.</note></term> and does not know where he must go.

God sends a light in the middle of this night to enlighten us; however, this does not happen by means of the scholars and wise men of this world, but through a <term>simple daughter<note>This likely refers to the mystic Antoinette Bourignon (1616–1680), whose uneducated background was often cited by her followers as proof that her complex theological writings were divinely inspired rather than learned.</note></term> who never studied and had no other master than the Holy Spirit. Nevertheless, she speaks as rationally as the best philosopher, and explores and resolves the highest points of theology without even knowing what "philosophy" or "theology" are meant to be.

<summary>The author argues that because academic theologians are hopelessly divided, God has bypassed the learned elite to reveal the truth through an uneducated woman guided by the Holy Spirit. This "new light" is presented as the only way to distinguish true faith from the "fabricated" doctrines of men.</summary>

### To the Reader.

She essentially possesses all branches of knowledge in perfection, yet she has learned them through no human means.

This is evident from the letters she wrote to various <term>theologians<note>The original German "Gottesgelehrten" refers to those professionally trained in academic divinity.</note></term> and other learned persons, who remained, as it were, struck dumb and were unable to answer her. Her <term>style<note>original: "Stylus"</note></term> is simple and consistent, yet grounded in such persuasive speech and firm truth that everyone must confess to being overcome by it. Her word is like a two-edged sword that spares no one, is impartial, and respects no human agendas; it is as a fountain of truth that always wells up and never runs dry. We do not have the <term>principles<note>original: "Principia"</note></term> of her <term>divinity<note>The study of theological matters or the nature of God.</note></term> in one general summary, but rather bit by bit in the letters written by her own hand, and here a part, through which various theological matters are treated in an unheard-of way, according to the true divine nature of the Holy Scripture.

<summary>The author explains that the subject's perfect knowledge is divinely inspired rather than learned, as proven by her letters which have silenced academic scholars. Her theological principles are not presented as a formal system but are revealed incrementally throughout her correspondence.</summary>

# Contents or Summary of this Present Treatise.

### The First Letter.

### Modern Theology is Entirely Contrary to the Wisdom of the Holy Spirit.

To a trusted friend, to whom it is explained in confidence that all modern theology conflicts with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit, and that those who consider themselves the wisest in divine <term>mysteries<note>In 17th-century spiritual writing, "mysteries" refers to sacred truths revealed by God that surpass human reason.</note> and hidden things are actually the most ignorant.

### The Second Letter.

### On Recognizing True Miracles.

To a Professor of <term>Theology<note>original Latin: "Theologiæ".</note>, adherent to the <term>Augsburg Confession<note>A document from 1530 that serves as the primary confession of faith for the Lutheran Church.</note>, who could not believe that a person could be instructed directly by the Holy Spirit unless they performed miracles. To which a very precise and thorough answer is given in all respects.

<vocab>Theology, Holy Spirit, Wisdom, Mysteries, Augsburg Confession, Miracles</vocab>

## The Third Letter.

### A true Christian belongs to the <term>communion of all saints<note>original: "Gemeinde aller Heyligen". This refers to the spiritual fellowship of all true believers, which the author suggests transcends membership in any single physical church building or denomination.</note>.

To a <term>theologian<note>original German: "Gottes-gelehrter", literally a scholar of God.</note> regarding various questions which he raised in his state of doubt and distress, seeking an explanation for the claim: that it is harmful for a true disciple of **JESUS CHRIST** to belong to a separate church, and that there are no longer any true Christians left on earth. Also, regarding the fact that many people were heard speaking of these matters as if they possessed the <term>spirit of prophecy<note>original: "Geist der Weissagung". In this context, it refers to the gift of divine revelation or the ability to speak as a direct messenger of God.</note>, while they meanwhile frequently contradict one another, and their actual lives do not agree with those of the prophets of **God**. To all of which a very precise and thorough answer is given in several letters sent to this same person.

## The Fourth Letter.

### That which comes from God must be held in honor.

To the same person, to exhort him that he must not despise an insight or revelation coming from **God**, even if he has never encountered anything of the sort before.

### The Fifth Letter.

->**God has given only one commandment to mankind.**<-

To the same person, by way of explanation: that **God** has never desired anything else from mankind than that they should cling to Him with their will; whereas all other <term>laws and commandments<note>original: "Geseze und Gebohte". The author differentiates between the singular divine will and the various religious laws that he argues were only necessary because of human failure.</note> of God took their origin solely from the sin of man. For **GOD** has never placed heavy burdens on people's shoulders, but they have loaded these upon themselves through their sins.

### The Sixth Letter.

->**He who is instructed by the Holy Spirit has no need of reading.**<-

To the same person, to show him that a soul who is taught directly by the <term>Holy Spirit<note>abbreviated in original as "H. Geiste". This reflects a central tenet of Radical Pietism or mysticism: the "inner word" or direct revelation is superior to "dead letters" or academic study.</note> has no need to read anything or to learn from men, because such things would hinder rather than promote the understanding of the **Truth of GOD**.

# The Third Letter.

### A true Christian belongs to the communion of all saints.

To a theologian <term>Gottes-gelehrten<note>literally "one learned in God"; a scholar of divinity or a member of the clergy.</note> regarding various questions which he raised in his state of doubt and distress, seeking an explanation for why it was said: that it is harmful for a true disciple of **JESUS CHRIST** to belong to a separate church <note>The author is likely addressing the "Separatist" movement within Radical Pietism, where individuals left established state churches to form private devotional circles.</note>, and that there are no longer any true Christians on earth; [and] that one hears so many people speaking of such things as if they possessed the spirit of prophecy, while in the meantime they often contradict one another, and their actual lives do not correspond in deed with those of the prophets of **God**. # The Fifth Letter.

### God has given humanity only one commandment.

To the same person <note>the "doubting theologian" mentioned on the previous page</note>, by way of explanation: that **God** never desired anything else from human beings than that they should cling to Him with their will; conversely, all other laws and commandments of **God** took their origin solely from the sin of man. For **God** never placed heavy burdens upon the shoulders of men, but they have loaded these upon themselves through their sins.

# The Seventh Letter.

### The Devil transforms himself into an Angel of Light.

To the same person <note>the theologian mentioned in previous letters</note>, as a summary of the following letter: to explain to him that the **Devil** transforms himself into an **Angel of Light** <note>original: "Engel des Liechts"; a reference to 2 Corinthians 11:14 regarding spiritual deception</note> and deceives under the appearance of goodness and virtue itself.

# The Eighth Letter.

### Signs by which one recognizes true prophets.

To the same person, to explain what certain signs exist to recognize true prophets through **Scripture** itself, and how many false ones have arisen in these days who, through their delusion and imagination, deceive both others and themselves.

---

# Today’s Theology is the First Grave.

opinion, then I find them so contrary to God's truth that I can in no way give them my approval.

2. It is indeed true that they refer to the Scriptures and have many beautiful words, but the effect and practice of their teaching is not truthful; for they boast of possessing the **Evangelical doctrine** <note>In this context, "Evangelical" refers to the Protestant/Lutheran tradition based on the Gospels, which the author feels has been betrayed by its leaders</note>, while meanwhile their entire life and actions conflict with it. They invent so many interpretations and explanations of the Scriptures that nothing living can be found in them anymore. It appears as a mere history which must be told to the people so that they might keep it in their memory alone; alongside this, all the sciences of the schools are devised solely to string words together, by which one might coax people into a contempt for the Evangelical doctrine and grant them a wicked life; for if contemporary theology did not spare sins, no one in Christendom who wished to be saved would be able to rest peacefully in their current state and way of life. Everyone would clearly see that they could not be saved on such a footing, since the practice of Christians today is entirely contrary to the first Church that Christ established. But because one hears these interpreters philosophizing and debating so forcefully to distort the true sense of the Scriptures, everyone lets themselves be convinced that one can well believe and follow them; for they are regarded by men as learned, though before GOD they are ignorant. They bring forth so many questions, so many <term>Cases of Conscience <note>original Latin: Casus Conscientiæ. This refers to casuistry, the practice of resolving moral problems by applying general rules to specific cases, which the author views here as a way to excuse sinful behavior</note></term> (cases of the conscience) and so many explanations of the meaning of the Holy Scriptures, that it seems as if their theology were devised for no other purpose than to validate all kinds of sins,

8. From many letters that I have written to the theologians <term>Gottesgelehrten: university-trained scholars or professional divines</term>, my heart can see in how many matters we are divided from one another. ### 2nd Letter. Wisdom opposed to the Holy Spirit. ###

...might have a better way to judge by, in order to distinguish and experience where the Spirit of GOD <term>GOTT</term> resides, so that you might not be deceived by false appearances, nor build upon external means that serve only the unbelieving and ignorant. I do not wish to exclude the true miracles <term>Wunderwercke</term> of those souls who love GOD; for they would surely perform just as many of them in this time as the Apostles <term>Apostel</term> did in their lifetime, provided it were necessary for the glory of GOD, who will at all times and in all places fulfill the will of those who love Him. 

However, I have said all these things so that you may see that it is the least grace <term>Gnade</term> that GOD shows to a faithful soul in this world to have the grace to prophesy <term>weissagen</term> or to perform miracles, and that these things must be considered as nothing in comparison to faith <term>Glaube</term> and love <term>Liebe</term>, through which souls remain united with GOD. These people perform true miracles upon the souls of their neighbors: they restore their sight, health, and life; and with this philosopher's stone <term>Philosophischer Stein</term> <note>A legendary substance in alchemy capable of turning base metals into gold; used here as a metaphor for how faith transforms the "base" nature of the soul into something divine.</note> of a living faith and love, they transform earthly souls into the pure gold of Divine Love. 

These are the true miraculous signs that are meant to occur in the fullness of time: to test and prove the power of the Holy Spirit <term>Heiliger Geist</term> through the healing of souls <term>Seele</term>, which are far more worthy than mortal bodies. Therefore, I ask you, my dear heart <note>An affectionate address common in 17th-century Pietist correspondence.</note>, that you no longer believe that a soul is not subject to the Holy Spirit in a more immediate way, or that it cannot understand the meaning of Scripture <term>Schrifft</term> without having read it or learned it from men. You should no longer long for these external miraculous signs, for fear of thereby dishonoring the Holy Spirit and tempting GOD.

12. I had intended to let you see clearly that there are no more true Christians present, and to provide the signs to distinguish the false prophets through good speech and truth as clear as the sun. In the meantime, I shall call myself:

### My Heart,

In our house
at Amsterdam, the
30th of March 1668.

->Your humble servant<-

->**Anthoinette Bourignon.**<-

### 5th Letter: Contrary to the Wisdom of the Holy Spirit.

### 5th Letter: Wisdom Contrary to the Holy Spirit

## The Sixth Letter.

### He who is instructed by the Holy Spirit has no need of reading.

To the same person / to demonstrate to him / that a soul / who is immediately <term>immediately: *unmittelbar*, meaning directly, without any mediating channel such as books, priests, or rituals</term> instructed by the Holy Spirit / has no need / to read anything / or to learn from men / because such things would hinder rather than promote the understanding of the Truth of **GOD**.

->My Dear Sir,<-

I am sending your Bible back to you and thank you for the care you take for my perfection; however, I sense clearly that men do not know the ways by which **God** leads me, since they now wish to bind me to reading and other means which serve only to hinder my inwardness <term>inwardness: *Eingezogenheit*, a state of being "pulled in" or recollected in the internal presence of God, away from the world</term>. **God** has always taught me to rid my spirit of all kinds of images, reading, and imaginings, so that my soul may be simple and free to receive the inspiration of the Holy Spirit in naked simplicity and without the addition of any other mental representations <term>representations: *Vorbildungen*, pre-conceived ideas or internal models that can distort pure divine light</term>. Should it not then be better to obey **God** more than men, who seek to bring me onto a different path from the one by which **God** has led me until now? If I am not given agreement in this, it will be in vain for me to write or say anything further, for it would be held as altogether suspicious

The ninth is faith, through which we come to know **GOD**, the truth of all things.

The tenth is modesty <note>original: "Bescheidenheit." This term suggests a sense of proportion and self-restraint in one's outward behavior and inner desires.</note>, which tempers all our deeds and desires.

The twelfth is chastity, which keeps in check all kinds of sensual pleasures of the body and mind.

### 93
### 9. Letter. Contrary to the Wisdom of the Holy Spirit.

...his Church—which is his teaching—will never perish. To this alone, and not to the ways and changes of men, must one hold fast. Though they may shape the Church for the sake of its outward dignity and appearance, they are nonetheless nothing more than decayed members outside the teaching and practice of the Gospel <note>original: "Evangelii"</note>, in which alone the salvation <term>Seligkeit</term> <note>While often translated as "blessedness," in this context Bourignon refers to the ultimate state of being saved or eternal happiness in God.</note> of mankind consists.

8. Therefore, many deceive themselves to the highest degree, believing that they will enter into Paradise by the broad and level path of Hell—following the teaching of all the hirelings of the Antichrist—while meanwhile they reject the narrow and thorny path which **JESUS** Christ taught. This path will never become otherwise, even if men change it. For all eternity, He will not change His law and teaching.

9. Since this is now certain, who then dares to live and die while imagining <note>The original German "vorstehen lasset" implies a false assumption or "letting oneself believe."</note> that they will enjoy salvation, even though they do not do what **JESUS** Christ taught in His Gospel <note>original: "Evangelio"</note>? Instead, they follow human teaching and practice which strives against the truth of the Gospel. # The Eleventh Letter.

### The Law of the Love of God is Necessary for Salvation.

->To the same person / to explain to him / that people / who love themselves / cannot love God.<-

->**My Heart/**<-

<margin>1.</margin>
It grieves me greatly to see and hear / that people say and believe / they love **God** / when they love nothing other than themselves; on the other hand, the commandment to love **God** is absolutely necessary for salvation / so much so / that no one can be saved without fulfilling it. The teaching of the Gospel <note>original: "Evangelii"</note> is contained solely within this commandment / that we should love **God** / which is where true love consists.

2. But people today no longer love **God** / because they love themselves / and these two types of love clash too much with one another / and cannot exist together in one heart. Fire would much sooner survive in water / and find less conflict there. Nonetheless, it is such a highly necessary commandment / that one must love **God** with all one's heart / with all one's soul, and with all one's strength / otherwise one will not be able to be saved.

3. # Today’s Theology is the First Degree

## The Eleventh Letter.

### The Law of the Love of God is Necessary for Salvation.

->To the same person, explaining to him that those who love themselves cannot love God.<-

->My heart,<-

->1.<-

It grieves me deeply to see and hear how people say and believe they love God, when in truth they love nothing but themselves. However, the commandment to love God is so necessary for salvation—so much so that no one can be saved without fulfilling it—that the teaching of the Gospel is contained solely within this commandment: that we should love God, for it is in this that true love consists.

2. But people today no longer love God because they love themselves. These two forms of love conflict with each other far too much and cannot exist together in one heart. Fire would much sooner survive in water and find less conflict there. Nevertheless, it is such an urgently necessary commandment that one must love God with all one’s heart, with all one’s soul, and with all one’s strength; otherwise, one will not be able to be saved.

But if one were to thoroughly investigate the basis of these **alms**, then one would frequently find that therein lies nothing but a natural tenderness, or—what is even worse—a desire to be seen as generous and charitable; yes, sometimes even to persist all the more freely in one's **sins**, because one believes that one has done enough for **GOD** if one has given something to the poor for His sake. ### Modern theology is the first grave.

it could be possible that a single person of sound mind would want to embrace such a mendacious and dishonest doctrine. # 12. Wisdom Contrary to the Holy Spirit.
<meta>catchword: what</meta>

**Questions.** Do you have anything else to present? I am ready to satisfy you regarding it, provided it is done with a sincere desire to discover the Truth and follow it; for as far as precise academic discussions are concerned, they are merely vain, and disputing <term>Disputing: a reference to "scholastic disputation," the formal, logic-based method of debating theology used in universities, which many spiritual reformers viewed as spiritually dead.</term> is certainly invented by the Devil to keep the pious busy with such things. Therefore, I will not take it upon myself to speak elegantly, much less to contest anything; for I am inclined only toward inner rest and solitude; yet nonetheless, I am moved to bear witness to the Truth at all times when I discover things that conflict with it. I seek no opportunity to contradict anyone, but when such an opportunity arises by chance—just as our conference <term>Conference: a formal meeting for discussion or the exchange of views, in this context likely a spiritual or theological dialogue.</term> has done—then I receive it from the hand of God and bring forth my part, as much as God obligates me to do, and no more; for I desire to learn and know nothing else than that in which He wishes to instruct me.

Accordingly, you must not take offense at anything I have said, even if my words might seem critical. Rather, use it to your advantage, for it stems solely from the zeal of Christian love that God has planted in my soul. I am perfectly capable of remaining silent, but I have been stirred to bear witness to the Truth because I see that it is unknown and obscured. It is a bounden duty of righteousness, for which I live in this world and for which I was born. If you now reject or despise it, then you are an enemy of your own eternal welfare, which is the only thing I have considered here; for I know well enough that one should not hold such speeches if one wishes to please you or those like you, for everyone gladly hears what strengthens their own intentions and aims, but not <note>The text cuts off here; the catchword "was" (what) suggests the next page begins with "what challenges them" or similar.</note>

...came to Amsterdam. I was warned by one of my good friends that I could not have the said little book printed or distributed until it had been declared "good" by a censor <term>Censor: an official examiner of books who checked for heresy or disobedience to Church doctrine.</term> or overseer. This moved me to look back and to doubt whether I ought to subject writings inspired by the Holy Spirit to human judgment; and because I saw that I could not bring them to light there without punishment or accusation, I decided for this reason to travel to Amsterdam as a "free place" <note>In the 17th century, Amsterdam was famous for its relative religious tolerance and was a refuge for many writers whose works were banned elsewhere.</note> and to carry this out there, intending to travel even further afterward.

Thus, I have remained here in Amsterdam since the Month of Christ <term>Christ-Monat: an archaic German name for December.</term> 1667 until now, staying here through the express will of God, who works without ceasing in my soul for His glory and the salvation of others. 2. So that I may now satisfy your question as to whether I have changed my religion, I answer you with a complete "No," and I say that I shall never change. I was born in the Catholic, Apostolic, and Roman Church <note>By using these specific titles, Bourignon emphasizes her claim to the historical, universal Christian tradition despite her conflicts with church authorities.</note> in the Spirit of Jesus Christ, and thus I intend to live and die; I also do not know what should move me to change, since I find nothing better. To this very day, I still do not know upon what all these different faiths are founded, for I have never associated with a person whom we call a heretic <term>Heretic: a person holding an opinion at odds with what is generally accepted by the Church.</term>, and I have read even less of their controversies <note>original: "Controversien" — referring to the heated theological debates and pamphlets common during the Reformation and Counter-Reformation.</note>, about which I shall ask very little. I have been here for more than two years, but I have not yet heard a single sermon from them. Upon my arrival, I rented a dwelling behind some warehouses, in a place where there were six different dwellings, and in them lived people of six different religions.

# The Change of Religion II. Grave. <note>original: "Grab." This is likely a printer's error for "Grad" (degree or level), or it may refer to a "grave" or solemn meditation on the topic.</note>

Initially, I could not understand it, because it seemed very strange to me—so much so that I even decided to go to each of these assemblies once to know what was being done there. However, over time, GOD took this desire from me and showed me that nothing solid was founded therein. For this reason, I have never been to any of these assemblies, nor have I visited any of their churches. My neighbors have left me in peace, for here there is great freedom of conscience; everyone lives without punishment in the opinion that they consider best.

3. I did not think that the people were so well-mannered, affable, and of sound judgment; for in my youth, I imagined that all Beggars <term>Beggars: Originally "Geusen" in German/Dutch; a derogatory term for Dutch Calvinists that they adopted as a title of honor during their struggle for independence.</term> or Calvinists were like wild beasts and not human beings like us—especially since we are taught that they are wolves covered in sheep’s clothing. Many see and indeed confess that their religion is not right and is founded solely on human delusions; for that reason, they turn away from it and remain impartial, praying to GOD that He might allow them to see the truth.

...that there is no other **God** than the one they can grasp with their spirit. I consider this opinion to be **Atheistic**, for anything that can be grasped is no **God**. The true **GOD** is as incomprehensible as He is invisible to such a small understanding, which has grown very slowly and can be brought to an end by a "small flow" <note>likely referring to a 'flux' or a minor stroke</note> or a powerful imagination. No one has come to me regarding religious matters in whom I did not immediately discover the evil and the good that lay within. Therefore, no one need be concerned that I would be so inconstant as to change my **religion**, whatever anyone might say to me; for everything outside of **God’s** truth can be nothing but **darkness** and **error**, even if it were covered with beautiful speeches and godly-seeming arguments.

# I. Change is an Inconstancy.
<note>The original header "I. Br. ist eine Unbeständigkeit" likely uses "Br." as an abbreviation for *Veränderung* (Change) or *Bekehrung* (Conversion), continuing the theme of religious switching.</note>

It would be better to apply oneself to how one might become a true Christian, rather than seeking to learn the opinions of various religions, because there is only one **God**, one true doctrine, and one single true Church, from which Christians must never deviate.

I cannot believe that a single one among these **Reformers** <term>Reformers: figures like Martin Luther or John Calvin who broke away from the Catholic Church to establish Protestant denominations</term> or founders of new religions was governed by the **Holy Spirit**; and I fear that some impulses, or movements of the mind, or a sense of dissatisfaction caused them to change their religion and deviate from the **Roman Church**, in order then to establish congregations according to their own impulse. 

For if they wanted to be true Christians, they could have become so just as well in the **Roman Church** as elsewhere—indeed, even better—because she herself lives outwardly in better discipline than any others, each of whom follows their own opinion and remains entangled in disputes, but has no one to resolve and settle these difficulties. Therefore, one should not change from the Roman Church, even if she had retained nothing more than a civil and political status.

For this reason, I will never change it; it is better that one change one's **morals** <note>original: "Sitten" — refers to one's habits, character, and way of life</note> rather than one's location, for our evil habits follow us everywhere. It is more advantageous to hold fast to the teaching of **Jesus Christ** than to seek salvation and truth in outward religions, which can give us nothing without the practice of this teaching, in which alone the true, healing truth consists. ### Most esteemed Maiden,

->I.<-

Yesterday evening, I received yours from the 19th of March of this current year, and understood from it that you defend the two points of our dispute, concerning the Satisfaction of Jesus Christ, as well as the grace or <term>predestination|prædeſtination: The doctrine that God has pre-ordained who will be saved and who will be damned.</term> of the <term>Elect and the Reprobate|Außerwählten und Verworffenen: Those chosen by God for salvation (elect) or abandonment to damnation (reprobate).</term>.

2. I have noted very well how you take the one as much as the other; but the opinion given to me by **GOD** holds the complete opposite. You cite various passages from Holy Scripture to strengthen your <note>original: "Wahn" — This can mean fancy, delusion, or a fixed idea.</note> notion; but I hear that those who hold the opposite view—supporting <term>free will|freyen Willen</term> together with Satisfaction through our own good works—likewise ground themselves upon the same Scripture. They point to just as many, or perhaps even more, passages than you do to confirm their opinion. Therefore, it appears as if Holy Scripture alone serves to uphold the opinion of one or the other, but not to discover to us the truth of those things necessary for our <term>salvation|Seeligkeit</term>. For people do not apply themselves so much to recognizing what we must do if we wish to be among the number of the blessed, as they do to defending that party and opinion which they have chosen according to their own liking. By now, men have gone so far in this matter that I believe even if **GOD** Himself came from heaven to explain the truth, they would not want to hear it if it contradicted the previously adopted opinion which each person seeks to maintain.

### It is better to pray for the grace of God: II. G

...[you] must receive the heavenly kingdom as a little child; for the time has come that **GOD** will reject the wisdom of the wise and bring to nothing the prudence of the learned. <note>A paraphrase of 1 Corinthians 1:19: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent."</note> It is better to study how one may be submissive and devoted to **GOD** than to become wise in the letter <note>original: "Buchstaben." Refers to a purely intellectual or literal understanding of scripture without spiritual depth.</note>; and it is more advantageous to take from Scripture the qualities of a blessed soul, which **JESUS CHRIST** preached, than to take up doubtful questions. It is also more useful to pray for the grace of **GOD** than to quarrel in order to know in what manner He gives it to us; it is likewise more useful to believe that **JESUS CHRIST** came to redeem those who will follow His life and teaching, than to ponder how He paid our ransom or how He bore our sins. Indeed, those who are occupied with these "beautiful" meditations commonly possess nothing of the Christian practice of the early Church; for they [the early Christians] must have seen the merits of **JESUS CHRIST** far more clearly than we do, and yet they nevertheless toiled, suffered pain, and worked vigorously to follow the deeds and teachings of **JESUS CHRIST**. We have enough other reasons to love our **GOD**, who imparts so many benefits to us, creates us out of nothing, maintains us through His grace, and instructs us through His works, without it being necessary to hold the belief that **JESUS CHRIST** has "done enough" <note>original: "genug gethan." This refers to the theological doctrine of "Satisfaction," where Christ's death is seen as sufficient payment for sin. Bourignon argues that relying solely on this intellectual concept can lead to spiritual laziness.</note> for us. The grace which we have received at every hour from His goodness must sufficiently bind us to love Him, without any other motives.

**True Truth is in God Alone, II. Gr.**

->To one unknown to my heart.<-

### I.

All these texts of Holy Scripture <note>original: "H. Schrifft" (Heilige Schrift).</note>, which you cite here in writing as proof that **JESUS CHRIST** has accomplished everything and paid our ransom <note>original: "Lösegeld." I believe that you do the same to maintain your own opinion, and therefore you must turn to them, or others of their kind, who love disputes. As for me, I will choose no side of any human opinion, whatever sect or religion it may be, because I see that they are all stuck in error; for I know only the one Truth, namely GOD, who is not discovered through disputing or quarreling of one against another, but only when one submits their spirit in humility of heart and casts off all imaginings of the mind. 

Only then does one receive the light of Truth, which the theologians <note>original: "Gottsgelehrten." A term for scholars of divinity or professional clergy.</note> of our time do not seem to seek, but rather they strive to find people who might strengthen their undertakings and confirm their established opinions. For this, I am not at all suited, since I have determined to remain constant in the Truth shared with me by GOD, and not to deviate from it to agree with human opinions; for they are in blindness and do not take refuge in the source of Truth, which is GOD, but would rather [look] in the books [written] by mortals

<margin>5th Letter.</margin> True Truth is in God alone, whereas that which is written by men consists of staying within and following human structures. ### My Heart,

I hereby open my mind to you regarding the matter in which you wish to advise me: that I should remain here and not travel to Nordstrand <note>Nordstrand is an island in North Frisia (modern-day Germany) where Bourignon eventually attempted to establish a spiritual community.</note>. I believe that your zeal is good, and that you judge this advice to be well-founded because of the reasons you attached to it. First, you say: That I could reach my **perfection** <term>Perfection: In Bourignon’s context, this refers to "Christian Perfection," a state of complete devotion and union with God's will.</term> here through the company of learned and virtuous people. Secondly: That I would accomplish something useful if I exhorted or awakened to the good those who desire to have perfection. Thirdly: That the land where I wish to go is a place inhabited by **coarse people** who are inclined toward drunkenness, greed, and deceit. And I cannot doubt that all your words have some basis upon which you build a judgment—that it would be neither good nor useful for me to leave this city. 

However, I look upon all of this with a different eye. I note in the first point that no advantage can be brought to my soul through the company of learned and virtuous people, because I have never been able to learn anything from learned people; rather, God has shown me grace and allowed me to be instructed by His **Holy Spirit**. I must not exchange such a Master—who teaches more solid virtues than all the virtuous people in the whole world—for another. Socializing and fellowship with others serves only as a hindrance to me, even if they were visible and physical angels; for to the enjoyment of a pure communion with God, the intellect must [be cleared] of all other images <note>original: *Bildnissen*; this refers to mental representations or distractions that come between the soul and God.</note>

# ->Public Sinners are better / II. Grave<- <note>In Bourignon’s mystical theology, a "Grave" (Grab) refers to a stage of spiritual death to the self or the world. This header suggests that even blatant sinners are in a better spiritual position than intellectual hypocrites.</note>

...detached, and to hold to nothing but **GOD** alone; by which you may understand that social interaction with learned or virtuous persons can bring me no advantage, nor contribute anything toward my own **perfection** <term>Perfection: A state of total union with God's will, free from self-interest.</term>.

2. Regarding the perfection of others—your second point: I cannot see what advantage I could establish among them, since up to this time I have found no persons who truly wish to become children. Everyone possesses their own wisdom and wishes to instruct more than to learn; and because I have no need for other instructions, and they seek to learn nothing from me, it follows that our fellowship would be in vain and a waste of time. Therefore, it is better that I betake myself into **solitude**, until **GOD** sends me true children. He has made it known to me that I am the **Mother of the True Believers**, but I can swear that up to this time I have remained barren without any children. Many of those who have visited me are indeed of good will, but I cannot give birth to them in the spirit that has been communicated to me by **GOD**, because everyone is more practiced in the "letter" of the **Scripture** than I am, and they would rather be masters of the **Holy Spirit** than His disciples; they cannot sin through ignorance, but certainly they sin through far too much knowledge.

3. The women here are much wiser in the **Scripture** than the theologians of our own region, but I do not see that they live any better than many ignorant people: they rely on the reading of **Holy Scripture** without putting it into practice, just as if it were given to us solely to provide the mind with beautiful reflections or discourses on divine things—all of which is vanity and a useless pastime.

### Hypocrites are Offended by True Virtue.

To a trusted friend who was vexed to hear how many persons murmured against A. # Hypocrites are Offended, Part 2

...and nevertheless allow themselves to imagine that they possess the very best virtues. They make it a rule to learn to speak lowly, to dress simply, and to adhere very strictly to their community <term>Gemeinschafft: This refers to the closed religious fellowship or sect, specifically the Mennonite congregation Bourignon was critiquing.</term>; furthermore, they do not walk, eat, or drink with those who have been cut off <note>A reference to the practice of "shunning" or excommunication, where members are socially isolated for deviating from the group's rules.</note> from them, much less assist them in any way—even though all these things conflict with what GOD has planted in my soul. For this reason, we cannot truly agree. If there were any offense in me, I would be much more offended by their ways than they are by mine; yet God does not wish for me to take offense at another's failings. Rather, I feel compassion for them and pray to GOD that He would send them His light, so that they might discover and correct these faults. In my view, many of these people would notice this themselves if they examined their own conduct as closely as I do.

-> 2. <-

Certainly, those who truly seek to please GOD would not follow them, because no solid virtue is to be found in their aforementioned ways. For striving to speak lowly of oneself while the heart is heavy with pride is a great arrogance <term>Hochmuht: A specific term for spiritual pride or haughtiness, which Bourignon views as the opposite of true Christian humility.</term>, accompanied by lies and deceit. This pride consists in wanting to be seen as humble by others through lowly speech; and the lies take root because one frequently says what is false. For someone who confesses to being weak and having nothing good in them is often so proud at heart that they could not bear for another person to actually hold such a low opinion of them. Indeed, it would greatly displease them to hear someone say they possessed no virtues at all, or that they had not reached a state of perfection.

## The Wise Contradict the Truth of GOD.

->I.<-

->**My heart /**<- <note>Bourignon uses this term of endearment ("Mein Herz") for her correspondents, indicating a spiritual bond, even when the letter contains harsh rebukes.</note>

I have received your letter without a date, wherein you speak of the joy you felt in knowing me and in hearing the concise truth of my writings—which you yourself have sent to various persons, even in foreign lands—and also that they were likewise gladdened by them. For this, you rebuke me, as if I had set out too early to declare the grace shown to me by GOD, or as if I had claimed an improper title for myself. You cite that in Saint Matthew, Christ says: that one must call no man Father on earth, since only one is our Father in heaven; adding that Saint Paul forbids women from teaching in the congregation, and that you could not find in the Scriptures that a woman must come in the final times.

## II. Letter. On the Truth of GOD.

<meta>catchword: 3. What</meta>

...alone <note>This continues from the previous page's final word.</note> came from the fact that you encountered a person who might strengthen you in your own opinion; for if your satisfaction had indeed sprouted from the fact that GOD showed mercy to the world and sent His light to mankind through a daughter—just as He dispatched **Abigail** <note>In 1 Samuel 25, Abigail intervened with King David to prevent him from taking violent revenge. What at that time was a **spirit of light and truth** cannot now be a spirit of error and lies; for GOD is constant, and the **instrument** <note>Bourignon refers to herself here. She viewed herself as a passive vessel or tool through which God spoke, meaning any rejection of her words was, in her eyes, a rejection of God.</note> through which He gave this light has not changed at all since that time. On the contrary, He sends new **streams of grace** for it every day, indeed every hour and moment, by which I am assured that what was recognized as good in the beginning by so many different persons cannot have become evil without a change in the Master who produced it.

But such a thing may well have happened on the part of those who saw and heard it, and who—by virtue of the instability and impetuousness of their spirits—turn like **weathercocks** to every wind. By this, they sufficiently demonstrate that their curiosity was not to seek **Divine Truth**, but rather their own satisfaction and whims <note>original: "Triffken." This archaic term refers to personal fancies, hits, or minor pleasures rather than spiritual substance.</note>; but because they find themselves attacked by some truth that rebukes them, they strive to seize upon a few words so they might find cause to reject everything, and through their **darkness**, in which they wish to remain, to extinguish the **light**.

## II. Letters of the Truth of God.

...ly / finding the title *Mother of the True Believers* <term>Mother of the True Believers: "Mutter der Rechtglaubigen." 4. I have heard various persons here who said they were filled with the **Holy Spirit**. # The Sages Contradict
## II. Grave <note>original: "Grab." In Bourignon’s mystical framework, the "Grave" refers to the burial of the old, worldly nature or a specific section of her work *The Light of the World*.</note>

...powerful / and are unbearable to me). You will always find enough other persons who have a desire to **dispute** and make it their life's work. ### I. Answer to the first accusation, that I think highly of myself.

Since I am indeed humble before God, I will not be puffed up <note>The German *auffgeblasen* (puffed up) is a common 17th-century biblical allusion to 1 Corinthians 8:1, "Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth."</note>, even if you, or someone like you, judges me so. It would be difficult for you to prove this first point through people who know me and have associated with me in community, because all of them would rather serve as witnesses to prove that your first accusation—that I think highly of myself—is a lie, and that I have walked all the days of my life, in all my ways and deeds, in <term>self-deprecation [Kleinachtung]</term> <note>Literally "small-esteeming." In Bourignon's spiritual context, this refers to the practice of "nothingness," or viewing oneself as nothing before God.</note>, and have never sought after that which might have exalted me. Indeed, the thought has never occurred to me that the poorest child I have taken in might be lesser than I; and I have remained in this same mind until this hour. Yet you dare, despite this, to accuse me of <term>pride [Hoffart]</term> <note>An archaic term for haughty vanity or ostentatious pride.</note> and self-exaltation. I have had enemies great and small who intended to harm me with various faults, but they have never dared to reproach me with the claim that I exalt myself or think highly of myself. Their <term>malice [Boßheit]</term> did not rise so high as to accuse me of <term>arrogance [Hochmuht]</term>, as you do; rather, they were afraid of standing in shame if they leaned too far against the truth, to which so many people testify to the contrary.

...no dispute would be found between our two opinions: for the **Spirit of God** <note>original: "Geist Gottes"</note> can never contradict itself, nor be divided against itself. For this historical or imagined faith <term>Historical faith: A term used in 17th-century theology to describe a belief that accepts the Bible's facts as true but lacks the "living" or "active" spiritual power to change one's life.</term> can no longer save anyone; therefore, a living and active faith is always necessary to be saved.

Behold there the truth for those as I know them. But the others, who believe that they shall be saved through the merits of their good works, I hold to be just as far from the sense of truth as the first. For no one can be saved through his works, and God has no need of our good works; He has given us everything out of grace when He created us. Eternal salvation, for which we hope, is also a gift of grace, and He gave this to us for salvation during creation before we were capable of doing good works. However, for that reason one must not cease to put these into practice as much as is possible for us, especially since the corruption of our nature <note>Bourignon refers here to the "Total Depravity" or fallen state of humanity, which she believes requires constant moral labor to overcome.</note> requires such to the highest degree; for if...

...[if we do] not watch, fast, give alms, and pray, we can easily be ambushed by our enemies—the Devil, the world, and our flesh <note>A traditional Christian triad known as the "three enemies of the soul."</note>—because they all conspire together for our damnation; and if we do not resist them with force, we cannot enter the heavenly kingdom. Therefore, good works serve us as powerful means, but not such that they themselves can merit salvation <term>Salvation: German "Seligkeit," referring to the state of eternal happiness or being saved.</term>, nor that God has any need of them; for He requires nothing, but possesses everything within Himself. Behold there the truth for those who think that their good works will merit salvation, which opinion strips God of the honor of the grace of our salvation and gives it to men, who defiantly and audaciously believe that their good works can merit salvation. They think that God is thereby obligated and bound by their works, though these works can serve for nothing else but to heal our souls, or make them healthy, and to keep them in good condition—not, however, to enrich God or to obligate Him so that He must give them salvation. This is because we have an Almighty and rich God who gives everything out of grace and love, and not out of debt or compulsion; on the other hand, our souls are poor, powerless, and deeply wounded, so that they always stand in need of medicine or a wholesome antidote. # The Labors constitute the Second Degree.

...poverty <note>original: "Armuth"; the first syllable "Ar-" appeared on the previous page.</note> of the spirit is healed, the wound of gluttony cured through sobriety and moderation; the wound of lust through abstinence and purity; the wound of pride through self-denial; the wound of idle curiosity <note>original: "Fürwitzes"; refers to a meddlesome or presumptuous desire for forbidden knowledge.</note> through the mortification of the senses and desires. But whoever believes that God is obligated to him for his good works, or thinks to earn salvation <term>Salvation: In German, "Seligkeit," referring to the state of eternal blessedness and peace with God.</term> through them, deceives himself—just as those do who hold the opposite view and believe that they shall be saved through the merit of Jesus Christ alone, while also saying (as commonly happens) that God well knows our weakness, and thus we hope to attain salvation through Jesus Christ's merit, even if we concern ourselves very little with performing good works. This is a false imagination of salvation, just as, on the other hand, it is a pride of life to believe one earns it through our good works; therefore, I can give my approval to neither this nor that opinion, for they are both outside the true sense of Scripture and legitimate truth.

You have confessed to me that for a long time you were of the belief that Jesus Christ had accomplished everything, just as the Reformed <note>Refers to the Calvinist or Zwinglian tradition of Protestantism.</note> hold it to be, and that after that time, upon feel-

Thereupon I turned back to that place and stayed there for a while once more, particularly because I found great contradiction from some priests and clergymen. Thus, I am buffeted by all the winds of contradiction and suffering.

You, my dear heart, can easily estimate that during the roughly nine years I spent in the hospital <note>In the 17th century, a "Hospital" was often a combined orphanage, almshouse, and asylum for the poor rather than strictly a medical facility.</note>—where I had under my supervision a great number of people of all ages, conflicting temperaments, and various nations and lands, some of whom were very godless and of evil character, even driven by the Devil himself—I found every opportunity to endure contradiction and suffering. For nothing opposes virtue more than vice, and no one noticed my failings better than those vicious persons, so that they might cover or excuse their own failings by accusing another. And because I was the Governess <term>Regentin: the female head or directress of an institution</term> of so many imperfect and godless people, I served as a target, as it were, at which everyone shot. 

In the meantime, I remained for so many years in such a burdensome calling, and no one can say that they ever heard of any dispute in the aforementioned hospital. Regarding this, I should be able to show you a certain testimony given to me by the authorities concerning my governance and conduct, from which you would sufficiently see that you cannot say with truth that I am unable to endure contradiction, and that such a claim is a mere slander devised by you to bring me into contempt and the virtue—

# 14th Letter: Human Hearts Puffed Up. #
I iij
<meta>catchword: zwie</meta>

...opinion must stand shamed and silenced. I have always attributed such things to the **Spirit of God**, who brought them forth immediately <note>original: "ohnmittelbahr"; meaning directly from God without human mediation or study.</note> within me; and now you wish for me to fall into the delusion and believe that all of this comes from myself and my natural judgment. I would have to be a very intelligent daughter <note>Bourignon frequently refers to herself as a "daughter" or "child" of God to emphasize her humility and lack of formal education.</note> if I had discovered such a variety of beautiful truths without school or practice, without books and without masters. I readily believe that you gentlemen speak thus out of ignorance, and that neither one nor the other of you knows what the **Spirit of God** or the **natural spirit** is; nor can you distinguish what comes from **Nature** or **Grace**, because you are not sufficiently experienced in the wisdom of the **Holy Spirit**.

I fear my judgment might displease you, yet I will testify that it is perfectly true, and that you have never yet fundamentally grasped or discovered in what manner the **Spirit of God** works, or in what form the **natural spirit** operates. Because you do not possess this <term>touchstone</term> <note>original: "Probierstein"; a stone used to test the purity of gold. You wish to be counted among the masters, but it would serve your happiness better to be good disciples. So that I may now prove that I bear more love for your souls than you bear hatred for mine, I will explain here what the **Spirit of God** and the **natural spirit** are, so that you shall no longer err in this regard in the future. I will state what effects follow from one and the other of these two spirits, and how they must be driven. This matter is very clear and firm, and should be understood by all those who are willing to use their **Reason**; but those who do the opposite are like irrational beasts, for **Faith** and **Reason** alone make the distinction.

### Studies constitute the second grave. ###

...between humans and animals. To distinguish between spirits, I set this as the first sign and foundation: that the **Spirit of God** has this quality—that it is active and works in nothing else but divine and eternal things, or things tending toward eternity. The **natural spirit**, by contrast, is directed solely toward earthly and temporal things, because everything that is natural has nothing other than time and earth as its goal. **Nature** draws its pleasure from, and knows or values nothing else but, what accords with itself; and although man is a rational creature, he nonetheless has no more than the cattle if he remains within his **natural spirit**.

You will perhaps say that man is a much nobler creature than an animal; but I consider him much lesser and worse than some animals if he remains in his **nature**. For a horse has more strength than he, a bird more speed, a mouse more agility, a dog a better sense of smell, and so forth. Indeed, as soon as little chicks have come out of their shells, they know how to feed and clean themselves, whereas man would perish from hunger and filth <note>original: "Koth"; meaning excrement or dirt. Bourignon uses this stark imagery to emphasize the total dependency of a human infant compared to animals.</note> if he had no assistance and help from others. You will also say that man has more spirit, reason, and understanding than various animals, but I answer that he is much more miserable in this regard if he applies these spiritual gifts only to earthly and perishable things. For who can doubt that a bird is not much more blessed, seeking its food by hopping about, than a man who must labor to obtain <note>original: "Sliessung"; likely a printer's error for "Erlangung" (attaining) or "Geniessung" (enjoying).</note> the same? And who does not see that animals have less worry and more comfort being clothed in their own hides than humans can have in their clothing?

# 14th Letter: Human Hearts Puffed Up.

I v
<meta>catchword: So</meta>

Can one truly say with any truth that a person is more blessed because they possess more spirit, **reason**, and **understanding** to obtain honor, wealth, and amusement than an **animal**, which has no need for such things to find the herbs and seeds of the earth? These are prepared according to the animal's taste and require neither cooking nor brewing; they inhabit the fields with others of their kind, where they may take their **amusement** and **sensual pleasure** <term>Wollust: In this 17th-century context, "Wollust" refers to physical or carnal satisfaction and delight in a general sense, rather than exclusively modern sexual lust.</term> without fear or shame. Is it not a far greater good to have all of this in full freedom than to have to use reason and understanding to obtain it? For all these gifts of the spirit are merely the means to acquire what the animals can have without any effort. Look at what the natural spirit is capable of; and if you want to know whether **nature** rules the deeds of a person, you must only consider whether what they say or do tends toward earthly or perishable things. In such a case, you may well judge that they possess a natural spirit, and not the **Spirit of God**; for the latter never considers anything other than divine and eternal things. Therefore, when one sees people working to gain money, or to enjoy the **sensual pleasure** and **amusement** of this world, one can surely say that they have only a natural spirit, through which they can find neither God nor eternal life. For even though people often flatter themselves <note>original: "liebkofet"; literally to caress or wheedle, here meaning to self-deceive or soothe oneself with excuses.</note> and say they engage in **trade** <term>Kaufhandel: Commerce or business dealings.</term> to use wealth well, or practice and study books to use **wisdom** well, or labor to earn their bread—nevertheless, all of this happens for the sake of the earth or time. It comes from a natural spirit that wishes to clothe itself in the **Spirit of God**, which alone stretches toward divine things.

### The Studies make the Second Grave.
<meta>catchword: that</meta>

To please **GOD** and to care for eternal things proceeds from [the Spirit]; for nature cannot find its pleasure and delight in a **GOD** whom it neither sees nor feels, since nature can be satisfied by nothing other than what the senses can grasp. Everything that exceeds the senses is not suitable food for nature, any more than precious stones can be food for horses; for the nature of the one does not agree with the food of the other. The natural senses are just as little satisfied by **GOD** and eternal things as a horse would be satiated by precious stones; for a horse prefers hay and grass—the food that accords with its nature.

And so it is also with the natural spirit and the senses: they value natural and earthly things more than **GOD**, who is an invisible Spirit, or eternal things, which they cannot see or perceive with their senses. From this, one can draw a certain conclusion: that he who seeks or desires no goods or sensory delights has the Spirit of **GOD** and leads a supernatural life; and that he who seeks nothing but **GOD** and eternal things cannot have this from a natural spirit.

# Studies make the second grave

...learned people to answer / well mindful that **GOD** gives more <term>knowledge</term><note>Original: *Wissenschafft*. ### 14. Letter. Men’s Hearts are Puffed Up.

### Studies make the second grave.

I would have always answered you quite wisely and without doubt; for I do not need to leaf through a heap of books, as you do, to find in them what I should answer to all your questions, and what report I should give to others; since all my answers would soon be drawn from the fountain of all **wisdom**, for it is a **living source** that never runs dry, and on all occasions provides such clear truth that it cannot be contradicted. As for pious people who seek only to be enlightened and to find the truth, they will never say that I do not answer their questions specifically, because my **library** always lies in the center of my soul, and I have no need to read other books—which I never do anyway—as they would only serve as an obstruction to me.

Truly simple souls feel clearly that my words and writings are not drawn from books and schools, for they produce a completely different effect in their souls than the words and writings of yours and those of your fellow <term>theologians</term><note>Original: *Gottesgelehrter*. Literally "God-learned ones." Bourignon uses this term to distinguish between those who study God through academic means and those who know Him through direct experience.</note>: but you want to hear nothing of this, and would even wish to thrust me out of this **divine wisdom** to learn school rules and principles, so that you might dispute with me about things that concern neither my <term>salvation</term><note>Original: *Seeligkeit*. Refers to the state of eternal happiness or the soul's blessedness in God.</note> nor yours, but only human and diverse opinions, in order to draw me to your side and make me agree with you. In this, however, I will not follow you at all, nor satisfy your particular questions, because they benefit no one, and can only serve to strengthen contentious <term>opinions</term><note>Original: *Opinionen*. In Bourignon's mystical theology, "opinions" are intellectual constructs that distract from the simple, revealed truth of God.</note>, which I would rather drive out of everyone's understanding, if it were in my power, than to give an answer to them in order to uphold them.

# 14. Letter: Human Hearts Puffed Up.

K

If you alone had the desire to understand the **true meaning** of all things, I would never fail to tell you everything that I know; but this is not what you are seeking. Instead, you desire only a meaning that agrees with the **preconceived judgment** <note>Original: *zuvor eingenommenen Urtheil*. Bourignon is criticizing confirmation bias—the tendency to only accept information that fits what one already believes.</note> of your own mind, and you are unwilling to accept anything else besides it.

I have seen this through experience; for when I gave you an answer so beautiful and filled with **truth** that nothing more could possibly convince you, you nonetheless rejected it. You remained steadfast in that which your mind had previously embraced, without being willing to give place to **reason** or **truth**. But now you complain that I do not answer your specific presentations and questions, even though I judge it to be useless to answer them. I find that your **soul** is not fit to understand the right meaning, but is rather driven by a desire to catch me in my own words and speeches, should any opportunity arise. And such a thing is to be feared, because you oppose me without cause or reason; you extract evil from that in which nothing but pure good is to be found, and you treat as untruth that which is and is called **pure truth**. What, then, would you not have done—if I had given you cause or written something truly "evil"—to think and draw evil from it? My **writings** and words have no other end <note>Original: *Ende*. In this context, it means "purpose" or "goal."</note> than to loosen souls from **earthly things**, so that they might love their **God** and eternal matters. Despite this, you still find a way to take evil from them. What evil could one possibly commit by abandoning worldly and transitory things in order to love God freely and perfectly?

For that reason, I often asked my mother and other **blood relatives** <term>Bluhtsverwandten: immediate family or kin</term> when we would move to the land where the true Christians lived, until they finally laughed at my words and assured me that we were already in the land of the true Christians. All of this assured me that we could not be true Christians; however, I was forced to remain silent and to ask no more where the true Christians might be, because people made fun of me, and my parents said to others: "Here is a child who wants to go to the land of the Christians." <note>This anecdote is a famous part of Bourignon’s hagiography, illustrating her "innate" holiness and her early rejection of her family's wealthy, merchant-class lifestyle.</note>

# 14th Letter: Human Hearts Puffed Up

Meanwhile, however, you have persisted in this same practice for many years. The **Apostles** did not act in this way; instead, they went from one place to another after they had sufficiently taught the necessary things there. They then let **GOD** work in the souls where they had cast the **seed of the divine word**; they testified by this that they sought nothing on earth, nor a following, nor to be heard in any way other than what was necessary for their eternal welfare and not for sensory satisfaction.

You will perhaps say, just as your friend does, that I wish thereby to scatter the congregations <term>Gemeinden: the gathered communities of believers or specific church bodies</term> and abolish the sermons together with the various assemblies. I answer: this opinion arises because I seek only eternal things, and through the consideration of all these instructions and daily sermons, I can see that they [concern] only temporal things, personal loss, the delight of honor...

I recognize only two states in the world: either the **Spirit of God** or the **natural spirit** <term>Natural spirit: human reason and intellect operating without the guidance of divine grace; worldly wisdom</term> lives in us; and no surer proof can be found than that which is revealed through deeds. He <note>Referring to the Spirit of God</note> always brings this same Love forth in the places where He dwells, for otherwise He would be an unfruitful Spirit; and if He did not bring His gifts with Him into His dwelling place, He would be stingy and greedy. And were He separated from Love, He could not be God, for God is Love, and Love is God. These will gradually be able to come to the true Love and status of a right disciple of Jesus Christ; but those who say they are born again / find themselves still far removed from it / and those even further / who take it poorly / when one says / that they are no true Christians / for whoever imagines himself to be so / will never be able to become it. 

Of this Jesus Christ says thus / because you think you see clearly / you are blind / for if you recognized yourselves as blind / then you would see clearly. <note>A paraphrase of John 9:41: "Jesus said to them, 'If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, "We see." # 4th Letter: Human Hearts Puffed Up <note>original: "4. Br. Menschen Hertzen aufgeblasen." "Br." is an abbreviation for "Brief" (Letter). "Puffed up" here implies being filled with spiritual pride or arrogance.</note>
M
<meta>catchword: The</meta>

Human hearts are puffed up. Some do not wish to hear any talk of the **Devil**; others close their ears to anything that does not agree with their own opinion; and meanwhile, they nevertheless claim to possess the **Light** and **Grace of God**, which I cannot understand. Either I or they must be deceived in this matter; for if they were truly enlightened by **God**, they would recognize that they are not true **Christians**, and that the **Devil** holds great dominion over the spirit of man. Indeed, they would even hold their own opinions as suspect, and would wish to understand and know from others whether their opinions might not be better than their own. For this reason, I pity them, and I can help them in no other way than by revealing the marks of a **true Christian** and pointing out the **error** <term>error: In Bourignon's vocabulary, "Irrthum" (error) often refers to a systemic state of being misled by false doctrine or spiritual pride rather than a simple mistake.</term> that currently resides in those who bear the name of a **Christian**, so that they might recognize from this whether they are truly **Christians** and work for what is to come, or whether they are stuck in the **error** and **deception** of **Satan**. I shall apply myself to this task at the first opportunity. Meanwhile, I remain

->My Heart<- <note>original: "Mein Herz." A cordial, intimate closing common in Bourignon's correspondence, suggesting her words come from the core of her being.</note>

For he rejoiced when he understood that I believed in the heartfelt future and conversion of the **Jews** <note>Serrarius was a prominent advocate for the idea that the Jewish people would soon convert to Christianity, a key event in his millenarian timeline.</note>, and he thought that the **Light** given to me by **GOD** would confirm everything he had written about it and approve of his entire opinion.

However, after he perceived that I understood the matter in a completely different way, and I told him plainly that my **Light** did not agree with his, he began to quarrel with me and sought to trap me in my words. Yes, he even told me that I must speak just as he does, because he himself had the knowledge <term>Erkäntniß: a deep, spiritual realization or revelation</term> directly from **GOD**. This I could not comprehend, since **GOD** cannot be divided, nor can He contradict Himself as we humans do. Either I or he must be deceived in his light; but since

# The Disputations are of Two Kinds.

I would not have answered your letter if I had not understood that you intended to answer or refute the remaining pages of my letter against Serrarius <note>Peter Serrarius (1600–1669) was a prominent Millenarian in Amsterdam who initially supported Bourignon but became a fierce critic when she rejected his specific prophetic timelines.</note>, which seems to me a waste of time. I, for my part, will no longer lose it [time]; but if you write further on the same matter, you should expect no answer. People who weigh my letters and yours well will be sufficiently capable of seeing who employs the most reason and truth. 

If GOD finds me prideful, He will not reveal His secrets to me, for He resists the proud and gives His heart to the humble. Take from my writings whatever good you find in them; in doing so, you can do no wrong, for even if the truth came from the Devil himself, it is always good in itself. But if you think something evil is in them, let the evil go, since you cannot judge matters of fact through your imagination. # 15th Letter: Invented by the Devil.

...[humble] person who carries the same into work <note>That is, who puts grace or spiritual impulses into practice.</note> can be good or evil: and just as it is a good work to give alms through Christian love and for God’s sake, so too can the same work be done through mere natural inclination and the impulse of the Devil, who often stirs a person to do good for the sake of vain glory and human respect. No one searches the heart <note>Original: "Nieren" (kidneys/reins). A common biblical idiom (e.g., Psalm 7:9) referring to the seat of deep emotions and hidden intentions.</note> and tests the conscience but God alone. If He now sees that I exalt myself because of the grace received from Him, He will, without doubt, have such love for my salvation that He would strip me of it, rather than allow me to be His instrument at the risk of my damnation. It is written: *Judge not, that you may not be judged.* Therefore, I ask you, my heart <note>A term of endearment or intimate address used by Bourignon for her correspondents, common in 17th-century spiritual literature.</note>, that you do not judge what you do not know; for it is very difficult to distinguish where the Spirit of God makes His dwelling, unless one has lived closely and for a long time with a person who is filled with it, and can see the effect of their words in their deeds. For as far as beautiful spiritual conversations are concerned, the Devil knows more about them than anyone else, and the godless often speak very spiritually; likewise, carnal <term>fleischliche: Literally "fleshly," referring to those who are driven by worldly or physical desires rather than the Spirit.</term> men have written many spiritual books. And I have heard many people here speak so divinely as if they were angels; but because I have observed them closely in various circumstances, I have found them to be without any love, from which I discovered that
